# Use user-story-splitter

<!-- Generated by build_pack_guides.py from pack.json and the skills' own files. Edit those, not this. -->

Split an epic, feature request, or PRD chunk into independently shippable user stories with testable Gherkin acceptance criteria and a recommended build order.

**Reach for it when** Use whenever the user wants to "break this down", turn an epic or PRD into a backlog, slice a feature for sprint planning, or write acceptance criteria for a story.

## Install it

```bash
npx skilldrop-cli install user-story-splitter                 # Claude Code, your user folder
npx skilldrop-cli install user-story-splitter --project       # Claude Code, this repo
npx skilldrop-cli install user-story-splitter --ide cursor    # or kiro, codex, antigravity, copilot
```

It is part of the Dev team pack: [`--pack dev-team`](../packs/use-the-dev-team-pack.md) installs it with its neighbours.

## Ask for it

Say it the way you would to a colleague. Requests like these route to it:

- "Split this epic into user stories"
- "Break this feature down into independently shippable slices"
- "Turn this PRD section into stories with Gherkin acceptance criteria"
- "What's the right build order for these stories?"

Requests like these belong to a different skill, so it shouldn't answer them:

- "Write the product requirements document for this feature"
- "Write the test plan covering these acceptance criteria"
- "Plan the phased rollout of this schema change"

If another skill answers instead, ask for this one by name: "use user-story-splitter".

## Check what you get

A good result:

- **Every story is demoable to a non-engineer.** If the demo is "look at this table in the database", it's a horizontal slice — re-cut it.
- **Every acceptance criterion is pass/fail without interpretation.** A tester who has never seen the epic can verdict it. ✅ *"Then the order total shows the discounted price within 2s"* — ❌ *"Then the discount works correctly"*.
- **Dependency graph is a chain or shallow tree, never a web.** No story depends on more than one other story; if it needs two, the cut is wrong.
- **Assumptions are tagged, not embedded.** Every default the skill picked appears as a visible `[assumption]`, so planning can challenge it.
- **The epic is fully accounted for.** Everything in the input is either inside a story or named in "Out of scope / not covered" — no silent drops.

## Use something else when

- The work has no user-visible behavior (pure refactor, dependency bump) — write a task list, not stories
- The story is already small and clear — go straight to `feature-implement-loop`
- Estimating effort in hours/points — this skill orders and sizes by slice, it does not estimate
- Writing the implementation — hand the story off instead
